notes:
Account summary: large regional payments processor evaluating Dedicated capacity + Private control plane for PII-sensitive inference. Primary ask: deterministic throughput guarantees and tight tail latency SLOs for chat + reranking pipelines. Team: CTO (Aaron Li), Head of ML Infra (Sofia Martinez), Ops Dir (Evan Cho).

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (Jordan) — high-level requirements capture; asked for baseline TPS and worst-case concurrency.
- 2026-02-02: Deep-dive (SE: Priya) — observed current on-prem avg 250 req/s, peaks ~1.8k req/s during batch settlement windows; 99th latency currently ~620ms (unacceptable).
- 2026-02-14: Architecture review (Fireflies ff_20260214_3672) — discussed warm pools, quantized fallbacks, and model routing policies.
- 2026-03-05: Legal + Security call — raised KMS/HSM integration, evidence for SOC2 + ISO artefacts (drive links provided).

Use-case & technical requirements (shorthand):
- Workloads: low-latency chat (50-200 token responses), high-throughput reranking for fraud signals, periodic bulk embeddings for indexing.
- Targets: 99th percentile latency <= 120ms for chat under steady-state; p50 <= 35ms. Throughput baseline 500 req/s sustained, burst to 2,000 req/s for 10-15min windows.
- Availability/SLA: target 99.95% monthly uptime for inference endpoints; tail-latency SLOs with clear credit calculation requested.
- Model preferences: open LLMs with 8-bit quantization for cost-critical paths; ability to fallback to smaller-distilled variant on capacity pressure.

Autoscaling & capacity management specifics discussed:
- Scale-up policy: trigger additional GPU nodes when request queue time > 30s OR avg GPU utilization > 70% for 45s, OR sustained token-generation latency drift > 20% for 60s.
- Warm-pool strategy: maintain a warm-pool of pre-initialized model workers equal to ~15% of expected peak (initial proposal: 12 GPUs warm, adjustable after POC). Warm pool to keep KV cache primed for commonly requested prefixes.
- Scale-down: cool-down 15 minutes after last high-util signal; prefer draining requests via queue rather than abrupt termination to preserve 99th latency.
- Cold-start observations: instance spin-up + model load ~90-140s depending on instance class; quantized checkpoints faster by ~30s.
- Queueing behavior: soft-queue limit at 300 requests (backpressure to caller), hard limit 1000 (reject). Implement token-based admission and graceful degradation (reduce max_response_tokens on overload).
- Burst buffer: propose short-lived burst pool (shared multi-tenant within their region) for irregular spikes — Redwood dedication must guarantee burst GPU capacity or fallback to smaller model variant.

POC scope & success metrics:
- 2-week Dedicated cluster provisioned in us-east-1 with 16 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for POC + 4 GPU warm pool.
- Load tests: 3 synthetic scenarios (steady 500 rps, ramp to 2k rps over 2 min, spike trains simulating settlement windows).
- Metrics tracked: p50/p90/p99 latency, tail token-generation time, queue lengths, GPU utilization, cold-start counts, cost per 1M tokens.
- Success criteria: p99 < 120ms for chat on steady-state, <250ms under 2k rps burst with warm pool + graceful fallback; <5 cold-starts per day during POC.

SLA negotiation points flagged by customer:
- Precise definition of 'unavailable' for latency-breach credits (p99 vs p95).
- Penalty formula: customer wants credits for tail-latency breaches (suggested: 5% monthly fee credit per 1hr aggregate p99 > target), Redwood legal prefers uptime-only credits.
- Maintenance windows: prefer monthly maintenance <= 2hrs scheduled; want blackout windows around end-of-month settlement (last business day).
- Data residency & audit: need proof of separation for POC logs and optional ability to ship audit logs to their SIEM.
